tasks.subject: Fix session `loaded` flag for unauthenticated/errored sessions
tasks.description: Critical auth-gating bug. `apps/web/src/components/session-provider.tsx:36-46` sets `loaded` only when `sessionData` is truthy, but better-auth `/get-session` returns `null` (not `{session:null,user:null}`) when signed out. Result: expired/revoked-session users (cookie present, server session dead) pass the server cookie-presence gate (`server.ts:111`), get `index.html`, then hang forever on `AuthGate`'s spinner because `loaded && !user` never fires. Same happens on `/get-session` network error (`retry:false`). Fix: derive `loaded` from query settled state — `const loaded = query.isSuccess || query.isError;` — and use `query.data?.session ?? null` / `query.data?.user ?? null`. Also fix the same `if (session)` bug in the example in `.trellis/spec/frontend/authentication.md §3`.

tasks.subject: Enforce BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in production (no silent dev default)
tasks.description: High security. `packages/utils/src/lib/env.ts:25` gives `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` a silent default `"dev-secret-change-me"` and `docker-compose.yml:25` mirrors it (`${BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:-dev-secret-change-me}`). A production deploy missing the var silently signs sessions/magic-links with a publicly-known secret → trivial session forgery (admin takeover). Fix: make it required in production via `.refine((v) => NODE_ENV !== "production" || (process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET && v !== "dev-secret-change-me"), …)` (or remove the default entirely like `ARGUS_API_TOKEN`). In `docker-compose.yml` use `${BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:?set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in .env}` to fail fast. Matches the README's "always override in production" with actual enforcement.

tasks.subject: Align dev server port with Vite proxy
tasks.description: High — blocks local dev. `apps/web/vite.config.ts:46` proxies `/api` to `http://localhost:3001`, but `apps/web/server.ts:139` hardcodes `serve({ …, port: 3000 })`. No `PORT` env exists anywhere. Dev API calls all ECONNREFUSED. Fix: make the port configurable — `serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000) })` and run the dev server with `PORT=3001` (or change the Vite proxy target to `:3000`). Align whatever side is wrong; the vite.config comment says the intent is `:3001`.

tasks.subject: Add top-level ErrorBoundary and catch-all not-found route
tasks.description: High resilience. `apps/web/src/app.tsx:1-29` declares four `<Route>`s with no `*` catch-all and no `errorElement`; `main.tsx` has no top-level `ErrorBoundary`. A render throw (e.g. in the Recharts subtree) unmounts the whole tree (blank page, no nav, no recovery); `/foo` and `/products/not-a-uuid` render an empty shell. Fix: add a top-level `ErrorBoundary` around `<App/>` (or per-route `errorElement`) with a fallback UI + "reload" action, and a `<Route path="*" element={<NotFound/>} />`. Data-fetch errors are already handled in-component via `isError`/`ErrorBox`; this covers the render path.

tasks.subject: Stop overwriting product currency with null on price change
tasks.description: High data integrity. `packages/prices/src/pipeline/check-price.ts:151-153` sets `currency: extraction.currency` on every price change. `types.ts` documents that `extraction.currency` may be `null` when argus can't determine one, so a single transient null clobbers a previously-correct currency on the product row and in subsequent alerts. Fix: mirror the `name` pattern — `currency: extraction.currency ?? locked.currency ?? null` (prefer the fresh value, fall back to the stored value). Add a unit test covering a null-currency extraction after a known-currency check.
tasks.activeForm: Fixing currency overwrite on price change

tasks.subject: Validate argus extract-price response with Zod
tasks.description: High rule violation. `packages/prices/src/pipeline/extract-price.ts:130-180` validates the argus HTTP response with ad-hoc `typeof` checks; `extract-image.ts` does the same. The project rule is "external API responses should be validated with Zod." The existing `priceExtractionSchema` in `pipeline/types.ts` is dead code from the old in-process AI pipeline. Fix: define a Zod schema for the argus `{ ok: true, url, available, price, currency, name, jsonld }` and `{ ok: false, reason, signature, retryable }` shapes and `.safeParse()` the payload, mapping parse failure to the right `retryable-error`/`terminal-error` decision. This also subsumes the "accept numeric price" fix (#18) since the schema can coerce/accept both string and number.

tasks.subject: Bound dashboard "latest reading" query (no full history scan)
tasks.description: High perf. `packages/api/src/modules/products/procedures/list.ts:60-77` (`getLatestReadingsByProduct`) selects ALL price_readings for up to 100 products with no `.limit()` and reduces to the latest per product in a JS loop. Unbounded as readings accumulate (100 products × months of checks = tens of thousands of rows per dashboard load). `products/get.ts` and `history/by-product.ts` both correctly `.limit()`. Fix: fetch only the latest reading per product in one query — a `groupBy` + `max(checkedAt)` subquery (or a SQLite `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY productId ORDER BY checkedAt DESC)` window) then `inArray` for those rows. Verify the `price_readings_product_id_checked_at_idx` index supports it.

tasks.subject: Roll back product row when checkPrice throws on create
tasks.description: High data integrity. `packages/api/src/modules/products/procedures/create.ts:51-60` inserts the product, calls `checkPrice(created.id)` (external argus HTTP), and rolls back via `db.delete` only on the three bad-status branches. If `checkPrice` throws (network/timeout/unhandled rejection), execution leaves the handler, oRPC returns 500, and the just-inserted row stays with no reading and no rollback. There's no `(userId, url)` unique constraint, so a retry creates a duplicate orphan. Fix: wrap the external call in try/catch — on throw, `await db.delete(products).where(eq(products.id, created.id))`, log a structured error, and throw `ORPCError("INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", { message: "Could not read a price from the page. The product was not added." })`. Do NOT hold a SQLite transaction across the external call (better-sqlite3 is synchronous; don't hold a write lock during a 45s fetch).
tasks.activeForm: Rolling back product on checkPrice throw

tasks.subject: Add index on verification.value for magic-link lookup
tasks.description: High perf. `packages/database/src/drizzle/schema/auth.ts:58-65` declares `verification.value: text("value").notNull()` with no index. better-auth's magic-link flow resolves the one-time token via `SELECT … FROM verification WHERE value = ?` → full table scan per login, and the table grows because nothing prunes expired rows. `session.token` and `user.email` are both indexed; `verification.value` is the gap. Fix: add `uniqueIndex("verification_value_unique").on(table.value)` (and consider `verification_identifier_idx` if better-auth also looks up by identifier). Generate + commit a new Drizzle migration.

tasks.subject: Add centralized 401/session-expiry handling in oRPC client
tasks.description: Medium resilience. `apps/web/src/lib/orpc.ts` `RPCLink` has no `interceptors`. `protectedProcedure` throws `ORPCError("UNAUTHORIZED")`; on the client this becomes a thrown Error → TanStack Query `isError` → generic `<ErrorBox message="Please sign in to continue" />` with no re-auth path. Also `useSessionQuery` sets `staleTime: Infinity` + `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so a long-lived tab keeps a stale `user` and never re-checks. Fix: add an `onError` interceptor on the `RPCLink` (spec `frontend/orpc-usage.md §2`) that, on `UNAUTHORIZED`, invalidates the session query (`["user","session"]`) or signs out, and navigates to `/login?redirectTo=…`. Consider re-enabling window-focus refetch (or a bounded staleTime) for the session query.

tasks.subject: Cap single-flight hold time for hanging extractions
tasks.description: Medium. `packages/prices/src/pipeline/check-price.ts:60-66` holds the single-flight lock for the full extraction; `extract-price.ts:35` sets `EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` with `MAX_RETRIES = 3`, so a hanging extraction blocks manual `check-now` for the same product and occupies a scheduler limiter slot for up to ~6 minutes with no overall deadline. Fix: add a per-product check deadline (e.g. wrap runCheckPrice in a race against a 180s timer, or reduce the effective retry budget) that aborts and surfaces a failure, and consider lowering EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_MS or MAX_RETRIES. Document the chosen total cap. Add a test for the timeout path.

tasks.subject: Retry on Telegram 429/5xx instead of dropping alerts
tasks.description: Medium. `packages/prices/src/notifications/telegram.ts:80-110` `sendTelegramText` catches all errors and returns; a Telegram 429 (rate limit) or transient 5xx permanently drops that alert with only a log line. Telegram rate limits are real. Fix: on 429, honor the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and retry once after sleeping; on 5xx, retry with bounded backoff (e.g. reuse `retryWithBackoff` from `pipeline/retry.ts` with maxRetries 2). Keep the "never throws / failures logged" channel contract. Add a unit test for the 429 path.

tasks.subject: Check image size before full base64 decode
tasks.description: Medium. `packages/prices/src/pipeline/extract-image.ts:288-292` runs `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` (up to ~13MB base64 → 10MB buffer) BEFORE the `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` check. A malicious/misbehaving argus can spike memory. Fix: check the base64 string length first — `const approxBytes = Math.floor(data.length * 3 / 4)` (minus padding) and reject > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES before decoding. Keep the post-decode magic-byte validation.

tasks.subject: Make first-user admin bootstrap race-safe
tasks.description: Medium (low likelihood). `packages/auth/src/lib/bootstrap-admin.ts:15-21` (wired from `auth.ts:50-55` databaseHooks.user.create.after) does `countUsers()`; if `=== 1` it promotes to admin. Two truly-concurrent first sign-ups can both insert before either hook runs, so both see `count === 2` and neither is promoted → zero admins. The comment claims it "only downgrades the second concurrent sign-up" but the real outcome can be no admin at all. Fix: use a single atomic statement — `UPDATE user SET role='admin' WHERE id = ? AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user) = 1` — so the count check and the promotion happen in one statement. Single-instance + magic-link makes this unlikely; still worth fixing.

tasks.subject: Track per-row pending state in Channels section
tasks.description: Medium frontend rule violation. `apps/web/src/components/channels-section.tsx:122-138` gates every row's enable/disable button on the shared `updateChannel.isPending` (all rows disabled during one update), and the per-row language `SegmentedControl` has no `disabled` at all so concurrent updates can stack. Spec `frontend/hooks.md` ("Per-Row Pending State") calls this the anti-pattern; `ProductList` (`product-list.tsx:18-24,56-78`) gets it right. Fix: track `{ id, kind } | null` local pending state like `ProductList`, gate each row's buttons on it, and `onSettled` clears it.

tasks.subject: Associate ProductEditForm labels and validate thresholds > 0
tasks.description: Medium a11y+UX. `apps/web/src/components/product-edit-form.tsx:50-62, 80-95, 119-123`: (1) `numberField(...)` renders `<Label>{label}</Label>` (no `htmlFor`) and `<Input>` (no `id`) for risePct/fallPct/riseAbs/fallAbs and the interval field — 5 fields with no label↔input association. `admin-settings-section.tsx:71-81` and `user-settings-section.tsx:64-72` do this correctly, so this is inconsistent. (2) `alertRulesSchema` requires those fields `z.number().positive()` (`packages/utils/src/lib/schemas.ts:44-50`) but the form has `min="0"` and sends `Number(value)` for any non-empty string, so `0`/negative is submitted and the user gets a generic `editForm.saveError` from the server. Fix: give each `Label htmlFor="…"` and `Input id="…"`, and validate `> 0` client-side before submit with `editForm.*Invalid` feedback.

tasks.subject: Make ProductList image lightbox accessible
tasks.description: Medium a11y. `apps/web/src/components/product-list.tsx:198-220` lightbox: (1) dismiss overlay is `<div onClick>` (violates semantic-HTML rule; spec wants `<button>`/`role="dialog"`); (2) close glyph `✕` and `alt="Product image"` are hardcoded English, not i18n (`product.name` is in scope and a better `alt`); (3) no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"`; (4) no focus move-on-open / restore-on-close; (5) no `Escape` handler; (6) no body scroll lock. Fix: render a real dialog (`role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`), move focus in on open and restore on close, close on Esc/click-outside, lock body scroll, use `product.name` as `alt`, and i18n the close label.

tasks.subject: Migrate TanStack Query keys to oRPC-generated keys
tasks.description: Medium rule violation. All TanStack Query keys are hand-written strings: `use-products.ts:15,21,28` (`["products"]`, `["product", id]`), `use-channels.ts:12`, `use-settings.ts:12,15`, `session-provider.tsx:14`. Spec `frontend/orpc-usage.md §7.1` explicitly forbids manual keys and mandates `createTanstackQueryUtils(orpcClient)` → `orpc.products.list.queryKey({input})` / `.key()`. Keys are internally consistent today (no functional break) but can silently drift from the server contract; `["product", id]` invalidation only works because the author happened to match the read key. (`["user","session"]` is the one justified manual key — better-auth session isn't an oRPC procedure.) Fix: add `@orpc/tanstack-query` dep, create `orpc = createTanstackQueryUtils(orpcClient)`, replace manual read keys and invalidations with generated ones.

tasks.subject: Harden Docker image (non-root + multi-stage)
tasks.description: Medium security. `Dockerfile:2,27-33` runs as root and `build-essential`/`python3` stay in the final image (bloat + compilers available to an RCE attacker). Fix: add a multi-stage build — build in `node:22-bookworm` (keeps build tools for better-sqlite3 native compile), run in a `node:22-bookworm-slim` (or `node:22-alpine`) final stage, and `USER node` (the `node` base image ships a non-root `node` user) so the process runs unprivileged. Verify the `iris-data` volume is writable by the `node` uid (chown in entrypoint if needed).

tasks.subject: Gitignore the root data/ SQLite directory
tasks.description: Medium footgun. `.gitignore` ignores `apps/web/data/` but NOT the root `./data/` that the default `DATABASE_PATH=./data/iris.db` creates. A dev running `pnpm db:migrate`/`pnpm dev` could accidentally `git add` their local SQLite DB. (Not currently tracked — `git ls-files data/` is empty — but a latent risk.) Fix: add `/data/` (and confirm `.env*` already covered) to `.gitignore`.

tasks.subject: Add security headers and cache-control in server.ts
tasks.description: Medium infra. `apps/web/server.ts:80-95,130-135`: (1) no `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, `Referrer-Policy`, or `Permissions-Policy` on any route. The `/api/images/:id` endpoint derives content-type from the file extension and sends raw bytes with no `nosniff` — exactly the sniffing risk it addresses. (2) `/assets/*` (Vite-fingerprinted, immutable) get no `cache-control` (browsers revalidate every load); `index.html` (SPA fallback) gets no `no-cache`. (3) Image endpoint reads the whole file into `Buffer` via `readFile` instead of streaming, with no `Content-Length`. Fix: add a `c.header` pass setting `nosniff`/`frame-ancestors`/`referrer-policy`/conservative CSP on all routes; `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on `/assets/*`; `no-cache` on the SPA fallback; stream the image with `c.body(stream)` and a `Content-Length`.

tasks.subject: HTML-escape magic-link email URL
tasks.description: Medium-low consistency. `packages/auth/src/lib/smtp.ts:41` builds the magic-link body as `html: \`…${params.url}\`` with no HTML escaping. `params.url` is server-generated (APP_URL + token), so low-risk, but an `APP_URL`/token containing `"` or `<` would break the anchor or inject markup. The Telegram notifiers are required to escape; the same discipline should apply to the SMTP magic-link body. Fix: HTML-escape the href and the visible text (or send the URL as plain text only).

tasks.subject: Fix check-now misleading "not_found" → "Product not found" message
tasks.description: Low UX. `packages/api/src/modules/products/procedures/check-now.ts:36-38` throws `NOT_FOUND { "Product not found" }` when `check.status === "not_found"`. But ownership is already verified at :27-33, so `not_found` here means the retailer's page is gone, not that the tracked product is missing — the UI thinks the product was deleted. Fix: return the `check` result as-is (the `create` flow surfaces `not_found` as a reason string), or use a message like "Product page no longer available".

tasks.subject: Allow clearing the Telegram bot token via the admin API
tasks.description: Low admin. `packages/api/src/modules/admin/procedures/update-global-settings.ts:37` treats an empty string as "leave unchanged" (`input.telegramBotToken.trim() !== ""`), and `admin/types.ts:34` types it `z.string().optional()` — `null` is rejected. So an admin cannot unset a leaked Telegram bot token via the API; they can only overwrite it. Fix: change the input to `z.string().nullable()` and treat `null` as "clear the column" (set to null/empty), keeping empty string as unchanged.

tasks.subject: Reset ProductDetailPage mutation state across :id changes
tasks.description: Low. `apps/web/src/routes/product.tsx:14-16,22-29`: `checkError` and `checkNow.data` are component-level state that survives a `:id` change (React Router reuses the same route component instance). Navigating from product A (with a check error or just-checked result) to product B shows A's stale state on B. Fix: add `useEffect(() => { setCheckError(null); checkNow.reset(); }, [id])` (and reset any other per-product mutation state) so the page resets when the param changes.

tasks.subject: Reset AddProductForm success banner + use shared formatPrice
tasks.description: Low UX. `apps/web/src/components/add-product-form.tsx:42-48,57-61`: (1) formats the "changed" price by hand as `` `${currency} ${newPrice.toFixed(2)}` `` instead of the shared `formatPrice` used elsewhere (e.g. `routes/product.tsx:109`). (2) `createProduct.data` persists after success, so the green "Added" banner stays while the user types a new URL. Fix: call `createProduct.reset()` when the URL input changes or on focus, and use `formatPrice` for the price line.

tasks.subject: Separate ProductEditForm pause/resume pending from Save
tasks.description: Low UX. `apps/web/src/components/product-edit-form.tsx:130-140`: the pause/resume `ButtonSecondary` calls `updateProduct.mutate({id, active})` but never sets `savedAt` (no "Saved." feedback), and `updateProduct.isPending` (also used by the Save button's `disabled`) disables Save during a pause. Fix: track a separate `pausePending` flag (or a local `pendingAction` like `ProductList`), set a brief "Saved." indicator on pause success, and only disable Save during an actual save.

tasks.subject: Make TelegramHelpTooltip touch/AT-friendly
tasks.description: Low a11y. `apps/web/src/components/telegram-help-tooltip.tsx:38-46`: opens on `onMouseEnter`/`onFocus` but the `<span role="tooltip">` isn't linked to the trigger via `aria-describedby`/`aria-labelledby`, there's no `Esc` to dismiss, no repositioning (can overflow viewport), and on touch devices `mouseenter` rarely fires so the tooltip may never open. Fix: add `aria-describedby` linking trigger↔tooltip, an `onClick` toggle for touch, and `Esc`-to-dismiss; consider a simple position guard.

tasks.subject: Add force-exit timeout to graceful shutdown
tasks.description: Low. `apps/web/server.ts:151-163` `shutdown()` calls `server.close(cb)` then `process.exit(0)` only inside the callback — can hang indefinitely on lingering keep-alive connections; a second `SIGINT` (user mashing Ctrl-C) isn't force-exited. Fix: add `setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 5000).unref()` after `server.close`, and re-arm on a second signal to force-exit immediately.

tasks.subject: Prices pipeline low-priority consistency cleanup
tasks.description: Low-priority prices cleanup (4 trivial items): (1) `packages/prices/src/notifications/dispatch.ts:60` `sent` overcounts — channels whose `send()` resolves count as "sent" even when telegram internally failed (it swallows errors). Make adapters return a boolean success or surface internal failure. (2) `packages/prices/src/pipeline/extract-price.ts` hand-rolls its retry loop with `backoffDelayMs`, duplicating `retryWithBackoff` from `retry.ts` that `extract-image.ts` already uses — refactor to use the shared helper. (3) `packages/prices/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts` wraps `checkPrice` in `pLimit(concurrency)` but `extractPrice` already has a module-level `pLimit(5)` — the scheduler limiter adds no throughput; document or remove. (4) `packages/prices/src/notifications/summary.ts:135` uses `Promise.all` (relies on `sendTelegramText` never throwing) instead of `Promise.allSettled` like `dispatch.ts` — make consistent/robust.

tasks.subject: Backend low-priority cleanup (return types, SMTP log, dead field)
tasks.description: Low-priority backend cleanup (3 trivial items): (1) `packages/database/src/drizzle/queries/users.ts:16` `getUserById` has no explicit return type while all sibling query helpers annotate — add `: Promise<typeof user.$inferSelect | null>` (spec: explicit return types for exports). (2) `packages/auth/src/lib/smtp.ts:35-46` only logs `logger.info("Magic link email sent")` on success; if `sendMail` rejects there's no `@iris/utils` structured `logger.error` from the auth package (breaks logging.md convention). Wrap in try/catch, `logger.error("Magic link send failed", { error })`, then rethrow. (3) `packages/auth/src/lib/session-cache.ts:14,24` keeps a `fromCache: boolean` ("Always false") purely to match the spec's Redis shape — dead surface area; drop it or document why callers ignore it.

tasks.subject: Drop build-time ARGUS_API_TOKEN placeholder from image ENV
tasks.description: Low infra. `Dockerfile:40-42` bakes `ARGUS_API_TOKEN=build-time-placeholder` into the image ENV layer. It passes `env.ts`'s `.min(1)` validation, so a misconfigured deploy (compose missing the runtime override) fails at runtime with confusing argus 401s instead of a clear "token not set" error. Fix: don't bake a placeholder into the image ENV — leave `ARGUS_API_TOKEN` unset in the image so `getEnv()` throws the clear "ARGUS_API_TOKEN is required" message when the runtime env omits it. (Keep `ARGUS_BASE_URL`/`DATABASE_PATH` build args as needed for the server:build step, but avoid leaking a fake token into the runtime ENV.)
